# Vendored from IC-ThermBench

`metrics.py` is a **verbatim, unmodified copy** of `utils/metrics.py` from
IC-ThermBench, retrieved 2026-09-10.

- Upstream: https://github.com/Day333/ThermalBench
- Paper: Hang, D., Yang, W., Ding, K., Xin, H. & Wei, J. (2026).
  *IC-ThermBench: An Open, Progressive Benchmark for Generalizable 2.5D/3D-IC
  Thermal Learning.* arXiv:2608.23977
- Licence: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 The IC-ThermBench Authors. Full text in `LICENSE`.
- md5 at vendoring time: `1585a2f94fa8f370e2cdd01032fc4fcd`

## Why it is vendored rather than reimplemented

Its own module docstring is explicit:

> This is the benchmark's only metric implementation: FNO / U-FNO / SAU-FNO / UNet /
> DeepONet / Therm-FM all call this one function, which is what makes the numbers
> comparable. **Do not write a second "equivalent" implementation.**

`docs/ic_thermbench_plan.md` §6 step 3 makes metric parity the load-bearing
prerequisite of the whole experiment: if our numbers are not computed the same way
theirs are, comparing them is meaningless. Calling their function gives parity by
construction, which is strictly stronger than writing our own and testing it for
agreement.

**Do not edit this file.** If it needs to change, re-vendor from upstream and update
the md5 above.

## Metric definitions that matter when reading results

Three of these are easy to get subtly wrong, so they are worth stating explicitly:

- **`rmse` is per-sample RMSE, then averaged over samples** — not pooled RMSE over
  all pixels. These differ.
- **`r2` is pooled** over all pixels at once. The per-sample average is reported
  separately as `r2_per_sample`, because fields with near-zero spatial variance drive
  per-sample R² to −∞ and drag the mean negative.
- **`max_temperature_error` (peak error) and `max_absolute_error` are different
  things.** The former is `|max(pred) − max(true)|`, the accuracy of the predicted
  peak *value*; the latter is the worst single-pixel error anywhere in the field.

`max_temperature_error` and `topk50_temperature_difference` are the two hotspot-oriented
metrics, and they correspond closely to what `scripts/hotspot_eval.py` computes
independently (`abs_peak_temp_err_K` and the top-1% recall family) — convergent design,
arrived at before this benchmark was known to this project.
